title: Redwood discovery - Atlas Systems - latency & throughput
summary: Discovery focused on p95 latency targets and throughput for streaming and non-streaming workloads; discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private, concurrency, batching, token/sec benchmarks and a proposed two-week POC/benchmark with Redwood Dedicated. Action items: send pricing and security docs, schedule benchmark run, provide benchmark spreadsheet and test plan.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-16 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Atlas Head of ML), Marco Alvarez (Atlas Platform Eng), Sarah Kline (CTO), Devon Reed (SRE)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, Liam and Nina from our SE team will run the performance side. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Good thanks, hey Maya. We want to focus mostly on latency SLOs, p95 numbers and throughput. we have a mix of streaming chat and batch generation, also some long-form completion.
[00:18] Marco Alvarez: yeah our production use is chat first, streaming responses to web clients, and then an internal job that does document generation at ~1k tokens.
[00:25] Liam O'Rourke: Great, that's right in our lane. can you share your targets? what p95 are you aiming for for short chat turns vs long completions?
[00:33] Priya Nair: For chat we want p95 under 250ms for 16-64 token responses at 75% concurrency of our active users. For longer completions (500-1k tokens) p95 under 1.5s is acceptable for us, but throughput matters — we need ~200 concurrent streams during peak.
[00:50] Sarah Kline: Important to note we do streaming so tail latency is sensitive, and we can't have large spikes. Also data residency and SOC2 matter — we'll get to security but want to validate performance first.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. quick qualifier — current infra?
[01:08] Marco Alvarez: We're on GCP, using internal Kubernetes with NVIDIA A100s for some workloads, but most of our inference is currently routed to a managed vendor. We're exploring moving to Redwood Dedicated or Private for predictable latency.
[01:21] Liam O'Rourke: OK. A few clarifying questions: 1) average token lengths for chat and doc gen, 2) concurrency distribution (how many simultaneous requests vs streaming connections), 3) do you need guaranteed p95 on 99th percentile token lengths or overall request time?
[01:34] Priya Nair: Chat replies avg ~40 tokens, doc gen ~800 tokens. Concurrency during peak: ~200 streaming connections, but active request concurrency is closer to 80-120. We care about per-request p95 end-to-end including network and chunking for streaming.
[01:50] Nina Patel: Thanks. On Redwood side we typically break down latency by model, sequence length, and hardware. For hosted we publish performance profiles; for Dedicated we can provision H100 pools and tune batching/async streaming for your profile.
[02:02] Marco Alvarez: How does batching affect streaming? if you batch aggressively you get better throughput but worse tail latency for streaming clients.
[02:10] Liam O'Rourke: Right, so we use workload-aware batching — continuous batching with latency budgets. For streaming chat we often use small batch windows (5-20ms) to preserve tail latency, plus prefix KV cache for repeated conversational context to avoid re-computation. For large doc gen we open wider batch windows to maximize tokens/sec.
[02:29] [00:02:30] Priya Nair: Can you give numbers? tokens per second, p95 for a sample model?
[02:34] Liam O'Rourke: Sure. For a medium-sized open model (30B equivalent, 8-bit quantized) on a single H100 we typically see sustained 600-900 tokens/sec for long generation with batching. Tail p95 depends on seq length and concurrency: for short 40-token chat we can hit p95 ~120-250ms on H100 with small slot batching and streaming enabled. On A100 it's a bit higher, p95 ~180-320ms. For 800 token doc gen on H100 with batching we see p95 around 700-1,200ms depending on concurrency and KV cache hit rates.
[03:10] Marco Alvarez: Those H100 numbers are promising; our current managed vendor has p95 ~350ms for short responses and 1.8s for long ones.
[03:18] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can provide a benchmark run using your prompt set. We usually run both throughput (tokens/sec) and tail-latency curves across concurrency points, and provide a benchmark spreadsheet. Liam, can you say more about the benchmark plan?
[03:30] Liam O'Rourke: Yeah we'll provision a small H100 pool and run tests at increasing concurrency: 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100. For each concurrency we'll run a mix of chat (avg 40 tokens, streaming) and doc gen (800 tokens, non-streaming) and measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory pressure. We'll also test with and without prefix/KV cache and with quantized model variants. We'll include a test for streaming chunk sizes (32 vs 64 byte-ish chunks) to observe perceived latency.
[04:03] [00:04:05] Devon Reed: For POC networking: we'll need to make sure outbound IPs are allowed and that VPC peering works if you do Private. For Dedicated managed, any special firewall needs?
[04:14] Nina Patel: For Redwood Dedicated we provide static egress IPs and can coordinate with your SREs for firewall rules. For Private/VPC we hand over the private control plane and you keep everything inside your network.
[04:25] Priya Nair: We also have an SSO/SCIM requirement and key management via our KMS. We need to verify KMS integration and whether logs can be routed to our SIEM.
[04:35] Maya Chen: We'll include SOC2 docs and our KMS integration guide in the security packet. we'll share a link to the security packet after the call.
[04:42] [00:04:45] Priya Nair: Back to performance — what about fallback strategies? if Dedicated capacity is exhausted during a spike can we fallback to hosted or smaller model variants?
[04:52] Liam O'Rourke: Yes, smart routing is supported. We can route by policy: first to Dedicated pool, fallback to hosted smaller model variant or different region. Also automatic model variant downgrade (e.g., 70B -> 30B quant) can preserve latency while degrading quality slightly. We can tune fallbacks per route.
[05:08] Marco Alvarez: In terms of cost, can you give rough numbers for H100 Dedicated versus hosted token cost?
[05:14] Maya Chen: We'll send a pricing sheet but ballpark: Dedicated committed capacity typically lowers unit cost compared to hosted per-token pricing, but it depends on utilization. we'll include a cost calculator in the deck.
[05:24] [00:05:25] Priya Nair: For our bench, we will care about tail variance across time windows too — i.e., p95 during a 10-minute burst vs steady state. can you measure that?
[05:35] Liam O'Rourke: Absolutely — we'll capture burst tests with sudden concurrency jumps and report tail-latency heatmaps and percentiles. We instrument per-token timelines so you can see where latency accumulates (scheduling, queuing, compute).
[05:47] [00:05:50] Priya Nair: Question on quantization — do you recommend 8-bit for our workloads? we worry about quality drop.
[05:56] Nina Patel: It depends on your eval sets. For many generation tasks 8-bit quant (and structured quantization) maintains acceptable quality with big perf wins. We'll run quality regression tests as part of the POC against your golden prompt set. If there's a drop we'll tune quant profiles or keep higher precision for critical routes.
[06:14] Marco Alvarez: How do you measure tokens/sec for streaming? is it per-GPU or end-to-end seen by our clients?
[06:20] Liam O'Rourke: Both. We'll report GPU-level tokens/sec and end-to-end throughput (tokens/sec observed by clients). For streaming, latency per token is important — we report first-byte latency and per-chunk latency as well as tail for whole request.
[06:31] [00:06:35] Sarah Kline: We have a hard requirement: interactive UI must feel <250ms p95 for short answers. can Redwood guarantee that on Dedicated?
[06:40] Maya Chen: With Dedicated H100 pools and tuned batching + KV cache, we can target that SLO for the short chat path. We'll validate in the POC and set clear SLOs in the contract for Dedicated with uptime/latency targets.
[06:52] Priya Nair: Great. we'd like to run two config experiments in the POC: 1) Hosted (baseline), 2) Dedicated H100 with auto-batching and KV cache enabled, and 3) Dedicated with fallback policy to hosted smaller model.
[07:05] Liam O'Rourke: Sounds good. We'll run all three and provide comparison dashboards. we'll include traces and token-level breakdowns in the Redwood Console export.
[07:13] [00:07:20] Marco Alvarez: What about sequence length distribution? our chat sometimes has longer context (1-2k tokens) which could affect KV cache and memory.
[07:22] Nina Patel: We'll capture your context length histogram and use that to size KV caches and choose model sharding/placement. For long contexts we may recommend pipelines with KV caching or context truncation strategies to preserve latency.
[07:35] Priya Nair: Any constraints about model support? we use an open model variant similar to Llama-3-34B (internal fork).
[07:41] Liam O'Rourke: We can onboard custom models for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we host a curated set but can bring your model into a Dedicated pool or Private deployment. We'll run compilation and kernel selection passes to optimize it. occasionally model names get garbled in our autoscribe but the SE will verify compatibility.
[07:58] [00:08:00] Devon Reed: For the POC run, what metrics do you provide in the benchmark spreadsheet?
[08:04] Liam O'Rourke: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory headroom, percent of requests that hit KV cache, CPU usage, network egress, and a cost estimate line. We'll share a sample sheet: https://redwood.link/benchmarks/atlas-2026 (we'll actually share after call).
[08:20] Priya Nair: we saw in previous benchmarks that bursty traffic caused queuing and increased p95 — do you do any queue shaping?
[08:27] Nina Patel: We support priority queues per route, admission control, and per-customer concurrency caps. Also can do graceful shedding or routing to fallback models when queue times exceed thresholds.
[08:40] [00:08:45] Marco Alvarez: small thing — in streaming we need chunk size to be tuned to minimize perceived latency. can you tune chunk size per route?
[08:47] Liam O'Rourke: Yes we expose chunking parameters and streaming window. For your UI we'd likely pick smaller chunk sizes for faster first bytes, then larger for steady streaming to be efficient.
[08:58] Priya Nair: about observability — we want token-level traces and cost breakdown by route. is that in Redwood Console?
[09:05] Maya Chen: Yes, Console has per-route token-level cost/latency, trace hooks, and you can export traces to your tracing backend. We'll enable a dashboard for the POC.
[09:13] [00:09:20] Sarah Kline: We also want to run a quality regression with human evals for quantized models — can you support that?
[09:20] Nina Patel: We'll run evals tied to prompt sets and surface regression alerts. we can also push diffs to your team and annotate examples with where quality dropped.
[09:29] [00:09:35] Priya Nair: Ok let's capture the concrete POC scope and dates. we want a two week window, start around 2026-05-25, run baseline hosted then dedicated, final report by 2026-06-08.
[09:43] Maya Chen: Noted. we'll prepare a runbook and schedule. we'll also include run commands you can execute from your env to replay traffic.
[09:50] Liam O'Rourke: We'll need your prompt set, a traffic profile (requests per second distribution and concurrency histogram), and sample client environment info.
[09:58] Marco Alvarez: I'll compile that and share by 2026-05-20.
[10:02] [00:10:05] Priya Nair: Can you include a test for cold-starts? sometimes scaling events cause cold tails.
[10:09] Liam O'Rourke: Yes we'll include horizontal autoscale and cold-start burst tests and measure tail impact. we'll include warm-up strategies and pre-warming recommendations.
[10:18] [00:10:25] Devon Reed: security quick note: we'll need to review SOC2 evidence, KMS flow, and audit logs.
[10:24] Maya Chen: We'll share the security packet (SOC2, ISO, KMS guide, RBAC docs) after the call: https://redwood.link/security-atlas.
[10:33] [00:10:40] Priya Nair: One more thing — can Redwood guarantee isolation of logs and PII for Dedicated? we prefer logs shipping to our SIEM only.
[10:43] Nina Patel: For Dedicated and Private we can configure log routing and data isolation. Hosted has opt-in retention controls but Dedicated/Private gives you full control.
[10:52] [00:10:55] Maya Chen: Ok recapping next steps: we'll send pricing and a comparison sheet, Liam will share the benchmark spreadsheet and test plan, Atlas will provide prompt sets and traffic profile, and we'll schedule the two-week POC starting 2026-05-25.
[11:08] Priya Nair: Sounds good. can you also include a sample SLA for latency / uptime for Dedicated?
[11:13] Maya Chen: Yes we'll include a draft SLA.
[11:16] Sarah Kline: thanks everyone, excited to see the numbers.
[11:19] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.
[11:23] [00:11:25] End of recording.

Notes/References:
- Benchmark sample sheet (to be shared): https://redwood.link/benchmarks/atlas-2026
- Security packet: https://redwood.link/security-atlas
- Proposed POC start: 2026-05-25; duration: 2 weeks
- Key SLOs discussed: chat p95 <= 250ms (40 tokens), doc gen p95 <= 1.5s (800-1k tokens), concurrency target 80-200, streaming first-byte latency and per-chunk latency measured

Transcription quirks: occasional mis-hearings (H100 sometimes auto-transcribed as H-one-hundred), KV cache sometimes appears as "KV cash" in earlier notes, speaker labels occasionally generic.
